24859-turned-adrift.title: Turned Adrift
24859-turned-adrift.creator: Unknown
24859-turned-adrift.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. steam service to South Africa was very different from what it is to-day. The steamers were small, slow, and infrequent; Natal was just then attracting a big influx of well-to-do people from England; passenger rates were high--as also, for that matter, was the freight on such special merchandise as was at that time being carried out to the colony--and those who took credit to themselves for their foresight believed that there was big money to be made in the sailing passenger trade.

arxiv-1812-10159.title: Trigonometry through Hopf algebras
arxiv-1812-10159.creator: Aaron Brookner
arxiv-1812-10159.description: Abstract . We consider various coalgebras and Hopf algebras related to trigonometry in this paper. In section 2 we answer the question of whether the trigonometric coalgebra can be defined to have the structure of a Hopf algebra, and over which fields.

arxiv-2009-01398.title: It’s Hard For Neural Networks to Learn the Game of Life
arxiv-2009-01398.creator: Jacob M. Springer, Garrett T. Kenyon
arxiv-2009-01398.description: Abstract Efforts to improve the learning abilities of neural networks have focused mostly on the role of optimization methods rather than on weight initializations. Recent findings, however, suggest that neural networks rely on lucky random initial weights of subnetworks called “lottery tickets” that converge quickly to a solution [ 8 ] .

arxiv-2202-00837.title: Topological Transcendental Fields Thanks: This paper is dedicated to Alf van der Poorten who introduced the second author to transcendental number theory. The second author also thanks John Loxton for suggesting he look at topological transcendental fields. The first author’s research is supported b
arxiv-2202-00837.creator: Taboka Prince Chalebgwa and Sidney A. Morris
arxiv-2202-00837.description: Abstract . This article initiates the study of topological transcendental fields 𝔽 \mathbb{F} which are subfields of the topological field ℂ \mathbb{C} of all complex numbers such that 𝔽 \mathbb{F} consists of only rational numbers and a nonempty set of transcendental numbers.

arxiv-2205-05961.title: Subgroup discovery of Parkinson’s Disease by utilizing a multi-modal smart device system
arxiv-2205-05961.creator: Catharina Marie van Alen, Alexander Brenner, Tobias Warnecke, Julian Varghese
arxiv-2205-05961.description: Abstract In recent years, sensors from smart consumer devices have shown great diagnostic potential in movement disorders. In this context, data modalities such as electronic questionnaires, hand movement and voice captures have successfully captured biomarkers and allowed discrimination between Parkinson’s disease (PD) and healthy controls (HC) or differential diagnosis (DD).

arxiv-2208-01753.title: Two-Stream Transformer Architecture for Long Form Video Understanding
arxiv-2208-01753.creator: Edward Fish, Jon Weinbren, Andrew Gilbert
arxiv-2208-01753.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Edward Fish, Jon Weinbren, Andrew Gilbert. Pure vision transformer architectures are highly effective for short video classification and action recognition tasks. However, due to the quadratic complexity of self attention and lack of inductive bias, transformers are resource intensive and suffer from data inefficiencies. Long form video understanding tasks amplify data and memory efficiency problems in transformers making current approaches unfeasible to implement on data or memory restricted domains.

arxiv-2310-00103.title: Linkage principle for small quantum groups Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification. 16T05, 17B37, 22E47, 17B10, 20G05. Key words. Quantum groups, Nichols algebras, Weyl groupoid, Root system, Representation theory Thanks: This work is partially supported by CONICET PIP 11220200102916CO, Fonc
arxiv-2310-00103.creator: Cristian Vay
arxiv-2310-00103.description: Abstract . We consider small quantum groups with root systems of Cartan, super and modular type, among others. These are constructed as Drinfeld doubles of finite-dimensional Nichols algebras of diagonal type. We prove a linkage principle for them by adapting techniques from the work of Andersen, Jantzen and Soergel in the context of small quantum groups at roots of unity.

arxiv-2312-08167.title: Quantum tachyonic preheating, revisited
arxiv-2312-08167.creator: Anders Tranberg, Gerhard Ungersbäck
arxiv-2312-08167.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Anders Tranberg, Gerhard Ungersbäck. In certain models of inflation, the postinflationary reheating of the Universe is not primarily due to perturbative decay of the inflaton field into particles, but proceeds through a tachyonic instability. In the process, long-wavelength modes of an unstable field, which is often distinct from the inflaton itself, acquire very large occupation numbers, which are subsequently redistributed into a thermal equilibrium state.

arxiv-2411-08978.title: What Rogue Hydrogen Clouds tell us about Galactic Magnetic Fields
arxiv-2411-08978.creator: Bailey M. Forster, Tyler J. Foster, Roland Kothes, Alex S. Hill, Jo-Anne C. Brown
arxiv-2411-08978.description: Abstract Observations of the Milky Way and external galaxies support the idea that large-scale magnetic fields are concentrated in galactic disks, with halo magnetic fields at least an order of magnitude weaker. However, very little is known about the transition between the two.

arxiv-2505-01100.title: Meteoroid rotation and quasi-periodic brightness variation of meteor light curves
arxiv-2505-01100.creator: Salvatore Mancuso 1 , Dario Barghini 1 and Daniele Gardiol
arxiv-2505-01100.description: Abstract Meteor light curves are sometimes known to display flickering: rapid, quasi-periodic variations in brightness. This effect is generally attributed to the rotational modulation of the ablation rate, which is caused by the time-varying cross section area presented by a nonspherical rotating meteoroid to the oncoming airflow.

arxiv-2508-20023.title: Tip of the Red Giant Branch Distances to NGC 1316, NGC 1380, NGC 1404, & NGC 4457: A Pilot Study of a Parallel Distance Ladder Using Type Ia Supernovae in Early-Type Host Galaxies Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2508-20023.creator: Max J. B. Newman, Conor Larison, Saurabh W. Jha, Kristen B. W. McQuinn, Evan D. Skillman, Andrew E. Dolphin, Mi Dai, D. Andrew Howell, Curtis McCully, K. Azalee Bostroem, Daichi Hiramatsu, Craig Pellegrino, Estefania Padilla Gonzalez
arxiv-2508-20023.description: Abstract Though type-Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are found in all types of galaxies, recent local Hubble constant measurements have disfavored using SNe Ia in early-type or quiescent galaxies, aiming instead for better consistency with SNe Ia in star-forming, late-type host galaxies calibrated by Cepheid distances.

pmc-11713583.title: Prognostic Significance of Visit‐to‐visit Blood Pressure Variability for Cognitive Outcomes, Vascular Events, and All‐Cause Mortality in a Memory‐Clinic Cohort
pmc-11713583.creator: Jiangbo Cui, Saima Hilal, Christopher Chen
pmc-11713583.description: BackgroundThe clinical relevance of visit‐to‐visit blood pressure variability (BPV) remains unclear in the memory‐clinic setting. We aimed to investigate the prognostic significance of BPV for cognitive outcomes, vascular events, and all‐cause mortality in a memory‐clinic population.MethodThe study included 590 participants from an ongoing longitudinal memory clinic study who had ≥ 3 annual visits and a baseline MRI scan.

pmc-12118161.title: Neonatal hepatitis B vaccination: Reevaluating timing and adjuvants for enhanced safety and effectiveness
pmc-12118161.creator: Aleksandar Cirovic, Ana Cirovic, Ana Ivanovski, Petar Ivanovski
pmc-12118161.description: Our aim is an achievement of a 100 percent vaccination rate without toxic vaccine effects. We did a comprehensive literature review on aluminum neurotoxicity and early neonatal hepatitis B vaccination. We analyzed indications for introduction of early neonatal hepatitis B vaccination and the data on experimental and clinical aluminum‐induced neurotoxicity.

pmc-12599395.title: Ex-situ generation of gaseous nitriles in two-chamber glassware for facile haloacetimidate synthesis
pmc-12599395.creator: Nikolai B Akselvoll, Jonas T Larsen, Christian M Pedersen, John A Murphy
pmc-12599395.description: The synthesis of fluorinated haloacetimidates relies on the access to the corresponding fluoroacetonitriles, which are toxic gaseous molecules difficult to store and handle. In this work we develop a safe two-chamber method for the ex-situ generation of these reagents in one chamber and their subsequent reaction with O-nucleophiles in the second chamber.

pmc-12701855.title: Immunohistochemical evaluation of T cell receptor and T cell receptor beta constant 1 expression distinguishes benign and neoplastic immature T-cell populations and reveals discrete TRBC1/TCR phenotypes
pmc-12701855.creator: Sahil Chaudhary, Elizabeth L. Courville, Jeffrey Craig, Vanessa Smith, Margaret Moore
pmc-12701855.description: BackgroundExpression of TRBC1 and TRBC2 is increasingly assessed in the evaluation for clonal T-cell populations. While flow cytometry has repeatedly shown utility in evaluating TRBC 1/2 expression, immunohistochemical (IHC) methods have not been extensively examined, particularly in immature T-cell populations.PurposeThis study evaluated TRBC1 IHC staining in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue, encompassing benign thymic tissue, thymomas, and T-lymphoblastic leukemias/lymphomas (T-LL).

pmc-12913380.title: Demographic and other correlates of non-prescription drug use among college students during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-12913380.creator: Subi Gandhi, Sidketa Fofana, Md Rafiul Islam, Tamer Oraby
pmc-12913380.description: Background and objectivesSubstance use among college students in the U.S. remains a pressing concern and may have intensified during the COVID-19 pandemic due to increased stress, uncertainty, and academic disruptions. This study investigates the relationship between non-prescription drug use and various demographic, mental health, and behavioral factors among college students during the pandemic's early stages.

pmc-13116751.title: Acute Aortic Dissection in Women: A Comprehensive Review of Sex-Specific Differences, Clinical Management, and Outcomes
pmc-13116751.creator: Vasiliki Androutsopoulou, Dimitrios E. Magouliotis, Andrew Xanthopoulos, Kalliopi Keramida, Metaxia Bareka, Konstantinos Stamoulis, Kosmas Tsakiridis, Thanos Athanasiou, John Skoularigis
pmc-13116751.description: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency characterized by important sex-related differences in presentation, management, and outcomes. Although women account for a smaller proportion of cases, they typically present at older ages and more frequently exhibit atypical symptoms, hemodynamic instability, and complications such as pericardial effusion or tamponade, contributing to diagnostic delays and higher pre-hospital mortality.

pmc-13200014.title: The Design and Conduct of Cohort Studies of Peoples With CKD – International Perspectives From iNET-CKD
pmc-13200014.creator: Natalia Alencar de Pinho, Laura M Dember, Yosuke Hirakawa, Takahiro Imaizumi, Vivekanand Jha, Adeera Levin, Luxia Zhang, Johannes Benedikt Scheppach, Viviane Calice-Silva, Alejandro Ferreiro-Fuentes, Manisha Sahay, Maarten Taal, Roberto Pecoits-Filho, International Network of Chronic Kidney Disease
pmc-13200014.description: Prospective cohort studies are important for understanding epidemiology, associations, and incidence of adverse outcomes of long-term conditions, including chronic kidney disease (CKD). Here, we draw on the combined expertise of the leaders of cohort studies within the ISN’s International Network of CKD Cohorts (iNET-CKD) to provide insights into the design and conduct of prospective cohort studies in people with CKD.

pmc-13466531.title: Immuno-Inflammatory Profiling and Complement Activation in Fabry Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13466531.creator: Mercedes Peña-Rodríguez, Nuria Bara-Ledesma, Martin Fabregate, Montserrat Morales Conejo, Fernando Domínguez-Rodríguez, Borja Merino-Ortiz, Sinziana Stanescu, Pedro Ruiz-Sala, Andrés González García, Amaya Belanger-Quintana, Mónica López-Rodríguez

pmc-13662278.title: A tripartite RpoS-CRP-cAMP-Cra circuit orchestrates metabolic reprogramming during stress adaptation
pmc-13662278.creator: Wenbo Chen, Yong Feng, Lin Liu, Rao Ma, Antoine Danchin, Conghui You
pmc-13662278.description: The alternative sigma factor RpoS (σS) governs stress adaptation in many bacterial clades, yet how it coordinates stress responses with metabolic demands remains poorly understood. Thus, by integrating RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and physiological and molecular assays, we redefined the RpoS regulon in Escherichia coli, expanding it to 667 genes and demonstrating that metabolic genes unexpectedly predominate over stress-response targets.

pmc-13685602.title: Pulmonary valve replacement-related change in biventricular global function index in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
pmc-13685602.creator: Shanique Sterling-Lovy, Francesca Sperotto, Lynn A Sleeper, Minmin Lu, Vedang Diwanji, Edward O’Leary, Anne Marie Valente, Tal Geva
pmc-13685602.description: BackgroundReduced biventricular global function index (BVGFI) is associated with adverse outcomes in repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF). The change in BVGFI associated with pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) is unknown. This study aims to characterize BVGFI following PVR in rTOF and identify pre-PVR factors associated with severely depressed post-PVR BVGFI.
